rules_evaluated.evidence: This dispatch (2026-07-26, second look) is the required fire. Trigger: 'forcing-function mechanic changed' — the file's committed fe18297 state had a drafted, pending {{prompt:walk-and-send-off-4}} fence as the intended fix for the prior REVISE; today's uncommitted edit abandoned that plan and instead removed the Phase 3 heading, folding its content into body prose with no new fence. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Reverses this file's prior pedagogy verdict (REVISE), which was written against a state where the fix-in-flight was 'draft and get approval for {{prompt:walk-and-send-off-4}}'. That plan was abandoned this session in favor of removing the '## Phase 3: Settle the tree before the send-off' heading and folding its (merged, two-bullet) content into the tail of 'Push back when a fill drifts from the codebase' (current lines 76-77), still unfenced. Two separate questions were in play and this pass keeps them separate: (1) SHOULD THIS BEAT BE FENCED? No — dispositively settled by 2f0c8a2 (2026-07-10), which retired the heavier fenced walk-and-send-off-4 prompt and replaced it with exactly this unfenced 'ask Claude to propose... ask to see the diff' shape; that decision is 16 days old and the body text folded today is verbatim what 2f0c8a2 left behind, not new roughness. §16's own removal test supports the same conclusion independently: cutting the tidy-up bullets does not collapse this module's teaching moment (the M4-underdelivers / M5-packages contrast), which is the definition of an optional refinement under §16's carve-out, not a mandatory teaching prompt. (2) SHOULD THE HEADING ALSO GO? This is a materially different question 2f0c8a2 did not answer — that commit KEPT a dedicated 'Phase 3: Settle the tree' heading/slide even while cutting the frame and the fence, so citing 2f0c8a2 alone as dispositive for removing the heading too (as the maintainer's note frames it) somewhat over-reads that precedent. The maintainer's note does supply an independent argument for the heading cut, though, not resting on 2f0c8a2 alone: 'the propose/review-diff move was already the third rep of the same pattern earlier in this same file (Phase 1 pick, Phase 2 audit, Phase 2 fill).' That argument holds on inspection — Phase 1, Phase 2's audit, and Phase 2's gap-fill each already establish an 'ask Claude to do X, then push back / review' shape via a fenced prompt followed by body-prose critique; a fourth instance of that shape, this one genuinely optional and lower-stakes (1-2 file moves, capped), doesn't need its own heading-level scaffold to land. Verified mechanically: slide-size (`scripts/check-slide-size.js`) and slide-numbering (`scripts/check-slide-numbering.js`) both pass clean post-fold.
